evolution_chain.description: Enacted as part of MICRA during a special legislative session addressing the medical malpractice insurance crisis
Current text substantively unchanged from 1975. Core dual-trigger structure (three years from injury / one year from discovery) intact.

case_law_documented.case: Sanchez v. South Hoover Hospital, 18 Cal.3d 93 (1976)
case_law_documented.doctrine: MICRA's shortened statute of limitations is constitutional
Discovery period begins at suspicion of wrongdoing, not certainty
Discovery requires knowledge of injury and cause, not knowledge of negligence

case_law_outstanding: Kitzig v. Nordquist, 81 Cal.App.3d 17 (2000) — fraud tolling requires affirmative misrepresentation, not mere silence
